summary: Not ready to merge: successive editor dictation sessions can appear in reverse order because lazy insertion reuses a stale saved caret. The phrase cutter, fixed Groq model, omission of language/prompt, failure handling and cancellation implement the main agreed behavior; the earlier startup/tidy cancellation findings are addressed. The diff against main preserves its unrelated features and leaves index.html and voice.html unchanged. node tests/verify.js and git diff --check main passed; npm test discovers the existing suites and all 25 task-04 tests. My browser run was blocked at Chromium startup by the sandbox (Operation not permitted), so I could not independently repeat the tester's reported 25 passes. I reproduced the ordering defect by executing the unchanged insertion functions in a Node VM with a textarea stub. Real Groq recognition remains unverified because automated responses are stubbed.
findings: HIGH — js/markdown/dictation.js:47-88: beginInsert() reads lastCaret.end for each new session, but emit() advances only the textarea selection and session.ins.pos; lastCaret remains at its original position while the editor is blurred. Reproduce with editor text 'Start end', caret at offset 5, then click the toolbar microphone, dictate 'First session.', stop and start another session without refocusing the editor, and dictate 'Second session.'. Also reproduce with the first response held until the second session is pending. Even when release() processes responses in capture order, the result is 'Start Second session. First session. end', violating the required ordering and spec section 6.2. Keep the saved editor insertion anchor synchronized with inserted text so later sessions inherit the advanced position, while preserving deliberate user caret changes. Add Playwright regressions for both completed and overlapping sessions after an actual editor focus/blur, asserting 'Start First session. Second session. end'. The existing cross-session test at tests/04-for-index-html-page-in-idee/dictation.spec.js:192 starts with an unfocused empty editor and exercises only append mode, so it misses this defect.
